source_text:
τὴν ἔχων, εἰ ἐξοίχοιτό πως ἁγιασμοῦ, συνδιολεῖται τοῖς ἄλλοις, καὶ συνυποκείσεται ταῖς ποιναῖς, αἵπερ ἂν ἐπιφέροιντο τοῖς τὴν ἀσελγῆ καὶ ἀνίατον κατηῤῥωστηκόσι ζωήν. Ταύτῃ τοι καὶ ὁ θεσπέσιος ἡμῖν Μελωδὸς, «Μὴ συναπολέσῃς, φησὶ, μετὰ ἀσεβῶν τὴν ψυχήν μου, καὶ μετὰ ἀνδρῶν αἱμάτων τὴν ζωήν μου, ὧν ἐν χερσὶν αἱ ἀνομίαι.» Ἄθρει δὴ οὖν ὅπως, «Οὐκ ἐξελεύσεσθε,» φησὶ, «τὴν θύραν τοῦ οἴκου ὑμῶν, ἕως πρωΐ.» Νυκτὶ μὲν γὰρ παρεικάζει τὸ Γράμμα τὸ ἱερὸν, τὸν αἰῶνα ἐνεστηκότα· ἡμέραν δὲ αὖ ἔσεσθαι προσδοκωμένην αἰῶνα τὸν μέλλοντα. Καὶ γοῦν ὁ μακάριος Παῦλος, εἰς τέλος ἤδη καταίροντα τὸν αἰῶνα βλέπων τὸν ἐνεστηκότα, λοιπὸν δὲ ἀγχοῦ, μονονουχὶ δὲ καὶ ἐπὶ θύραις ἤδη τὸν αἰῶνα τὸν μέλλοντα, προσεφώνει, λέγων· «Ἡ νὺξ προέκοψεν, ἡ δὲ ἡμέρα ἤγγικεν.» Ἀποθώμεθα οὖν τὰ ἔργα τοῦ σκότους καὶ ἐνδυσώμεθα τὰ ὅπλα τοῦ φωτὸς, ὡς ἐν ἡμέρᾳ εὐσχημόνως περιπατήσωμεν.» Οὐκοῦν τὸ μέχρι παντὸς τοῦ βίου κατασημήνειεν ἂν, τὸ ἕως πρωῒ, τουτέστιν, ἕως ἂν ὁ μέλλων ἀναδειχθείη καιρός. Πῶς δ' ἂν καὶ τοῦτο γένοιτο πρὸς ἡμῶν; ἐν γὰρ τῷ τέλει τῆς ἑκάστου ζωῆς, μονονουχὶ καὶ εἰσβέβηκεν ὁ μέλλων αἰών. Εἴπερ ἐστὶν ἀληθὲς, ὅτι δεδικαίωται μὲν ἀπὸ ἁμαρτίας ὁ θάνατον ὑποδύς· συνέκλεισε γὰρ ὁ Θεὸς κατ' αὐτοῦ, κατὰ τὸ γεγραμμένον, τετήρηται δὲ τῷ βήματι τοῦ Χριστοῦ, καὶ ὡς ἂν ἔχοι τῷ ἰδίῳ τέλει καταληφθεὶς, οὕτω καὶ παραστήσεται.
{ΠΑΛΛ.} Συνίημι ὃ φής· καὶ εὖ γε δὴ λίαν ὁ λόγος ἔχει.
{ΚΥΡ.} Ἀλλ' ὧδε μὲν ἡμῖν τὸ Χριστοῦ μυστήριον ἐσκιαγραφεῖτο τοῖς πάλαι καταθυομένου κατὰ καιρὸν τοῦ ἀμνοῦ, καθ' ὃν ἀληθῶς καὶ αὐτὸς ὁ Ἐμμανουὴλ τὴν ὑπὲρ τῆς ἁπάντων ζωῆς ὑπομεμένηκε σφαγήν· καὶ γοῦν ὁ θεσπέσιος γράφει Παῦλος, ὅτι τὸ «Πάσχα ἡμῶν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἐτύθη Χριστός.» Χρῆναί γε μὴν ἔφη τὸ θεῖον ἡμῖν χρησμῴδημα καὶ ἐν μηνὶ τῷ δευτέρῳ τελεῖσθαι τὰ ἱερὰ, καὶ τῆς ἑορτῆς τὸ σχῆμα διαπεραίνεσθαι δεῖν, εἴπερ τι τῶν ἀναγκαίων ἡμᾶς παραποδισμάτων ἐξείργοι τυχὸν καὶ ἀποκομίζοι τοῦ δύνασθαι πληροῦν ἐν μηνὶ τῷ πρώτῳ τὰ τεθεσπισμένα. Βούλει τὸ θεῖον αὐτὸ παραθέντες λόγιον, τὰ εἰκότα λέγωμεν;
{ΠΑΛΛ.} Πάνυ μὲν οὖν.
{ΚΥΡ.} Γέγραπται τοίνυν ἐν τοῖς Ἀριθμοῖς· «Καὶ ἐλάλησε Κύριος πρὸς Μωσῆν ἐν τῷ ὄρει Σινᾶ ἐν τῷ ἔτει τῷ δευτέρῳ, ἐξελθόντων αὐτῶν ἐκ γῆς Αἰγύπτου ἐν τῷ μηνὶ τῷ πρώτῳ, λέγων· Εἶπον, καὶ ποιείτωσαν οἱ υἱοὶ Ἰσραὴλ τὸ Πάσχα καθ' ὥραν αὐτοῦ, τῇ τεσσαρεσκαιδεκάτῃ ἡμέρᾳ τοῦ μηνὸς τοῦ πρώτου πρὸς ἑσπέραν, ποιήσεις αὐτὸ κατὰ καιρούς· κατὰ τὸν νόμον αὐτοῦ, καὶ κατὰ τὴν σύγκρισιν αὐτοῦ ποιήσεις αὐτό. Καὶ ἐλάλησε Μωσῆς τοῖς υἱοῖς Ἰσραὴλ ποιῆσαι τὸ Πάσχα ἐναρχομένου τῇ τεσσαρεσκαιδεκάτῃ ἡμέρᾳ τοῦ μηνὸς ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ τοῦ Σινᾶ. Καθὰ συνέταξε Κύριος τῷ Μωσῇ, οὕτως ἐποίησαν οἱ υἱοὶ Ἰσραήλ.
pass_a_gloss: (having as a sort of house the vir)tue, if he should somehow depart from sanctification, will perish together with the others, and will be subject together to the punishments which would be brought upon those who have been sick with the licentious and incurable life. In this way the divine Singer too says to us: Do not destroy together, he says, with impious men my soul, and with men of bloods my life, in whose hands are the lawlessnesses. Look then how: You will not go out, he says, the door of your house until morning. For the sacred Letter likens to night the present age, and the age to come to be the day expected. And indeed blessed Paul, seeing the present age already putting in to its end, and the coming age thereafter near and almost already at the doors, cried out saying: The night advanced, and the day has come near. Let us then put off the works of darkness and put on the weapons of light, as in day let us walk decently. Therefore 'until morning' would signify the until-the-whole of life, that is, until the coming season should be displayed. And how would this happen with us? For at the end of each one's life the coming age has all but entered. If it is true that the one having gone under death has been justified from sin; for God shut (it) against him, according to what is written, and he has been kept for the tribunal of Christ, and as he might be when overtaken by his own end, so also he will be presented. PALLADIUS: I understand what you say; and the argument holds very well indeed. CYRIL: But thus the mystery of Christ was shadow-drawn for us by those of old, the lamb being sacrificed at the season, at which truly Emmanuel himself also endured the slaughter on behalf of the life of all; and indeed divine Paul writes that 'our Passover was sacrificed on our behalf, Christ'. The divine oracle said that it is necessary also in the second month for the sacred things to be completed and the form of the feast to be carried through, if some one of the necessary hindrances should perhaps keep us out and carry us away from being able to fulfill in the first month the things decreed. Do you wish that, having set beside (us) the divine saying itself, we speak the likely things? PALLADIUS: Very much so. CYRIL: It is written then in the Numbers: And the Lord spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai in the second year, of their having gone out from the land of Egypt, in the first month, saying: Say, and let the sons of Israel make the Passover according to its hour, on the fourteenth day of the first month toward evening; you will make it according to seasons; according to its law and according to its rule you will make it. And Moses spoke to the sons of Israel to make the Passover, beginning on the fourteenth day of the month in the desert of Sinai. Just as the Lord appointed to Moses, so the sons of Israel did.
pass_b_english: Cyril: … virtue, if he should somehow depart from holiness, will perish along with the rest and will be subject together to the penalties that would be brought on those who have fallen sick with the licentious and incurable life. That is why the inspired Psalmist says to us, ‘Do not destroy my soul with the ungodly, nor my life with men of blood, in whose hands are lawless deeds’ (Psalm 26:9–10). See, then, how it says, ‘You shall not go out of the door of your house until morning’ (Exodus 12:22). For the sacred letter likens the present age to night, and the age to come, which we expect, to day. Indeed the blessed Paul, seeing the present age already drawing to its end and the age to come close by, all but at the doors already, called out, saying, ‘The night is far gone, the day is at hand. So let us cast off the works of darkness and put on the armor of light; let us walk becomingly, as in the day’ (Romans 13:12–13). ‘Until morning,’ then, would signify the whole of life, that is, until the coming season is made manifest. And how would this happen for us? At the end of each one’s life the age to come has all but entered; if indeed it is true that the one who has gone down into death has been set free from sin (Romans 6:7), for God has shut him in, as it is written, and he is kept for the judgment seat of Christ, and as he was when his own end overtook him, so he will stand there.
Palladius: I understand what you say; and the argument is very good indeed.

Cyril: In this way, then, the mystery of Christ was sketched in shadow for the people of old, when the lamb was sacrificed at its season, the very season at which Emmanuel himself truly underwent slaughter for the life of all. The inspired Paul indeed writes that ‘Christ, our Passover, was sacrificed for us’ (1 Corinthians 5:7). Yet the divine oracle said that the sacred rites must be performed in the second month too, and the form of the feast carried through, if some necessary hindrance should happen to shut us out and keep us from being able to fulfill in the first month what was decreed. Would you like us to set out the divine saying itself and then say what is fitting?

Cyril: It is written, then, in Numbers: ‘And the Lord spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai in the second year after they had come out of the land of Egypt, in the first month, saying: Speak, and let the sons of Israel keep the Passover at its season, on the fourteenth day of the first month, toward evening; you shall keep it at its appointed time; according to its law and according to its ordinance you shall keep it. And Moses told the sons of Israel to keep the Passover, beginning on the fourteenth day of the month, in the wilderness of Sinai. As the Lord had commanded Moses, so the sons of Israel did’ (Numbers 9:1–5).

choices.term: συνέκλεισε γὰρ ὁ Θεὸς κατ’ αὐτοῦ, κατὰ τὸ γεγραμμένον
choices.english: for God has shut him in, as it is written
choices.why: The phrase may echo Genesis 7:16 (the Lord shut Noah in); the source is not certain, so no reference is printed.
Cyril’s text of Numbers 9:1; the Septuagint has ‘in the wilderness of Sinai’. Translated as printed.

choices.english: has been set free from sin
choices.why: Romans 6:7 wording (‘justified from sin’, i.e. freed).
